condition.notes: Desktop CPU VCORE missing. Same first-step workflow as laptop VCORE: resistance first, then walk the sequence. CPU VRM rails have a very low normal resistance; compare against a known-good board.

next_steps.action: Unplug the PSU from mains. Wait 60 s. Measure resistance from VCORE to ground at the CPU socket VCC pins or the VRM inductor output pads.

measure.where: CPU socket VCC pins or VRM inductor output pads
measure.expected: Highly board-dependent — typically 5-30 ohm on a healthy desktop board. Compare to a known-good board. Values below 2 ohm with no load suggest a shorted output FET or output cap.
measure.safety: VRM rails hold charge in many ceramics — wait for full discharge before measuring. Unplug from mains, not just PS_ON# off.

interpretations.if_result: Resistance much lower than known-good board
interpretations.then: Short on VCORE. Suspect low-side MOSFET(s) or output cap. Do NOT apply power; hunt the short first.
No short. Proceed to check VRM input supply (CPU_VRM_INPUT, which is the EPS 12V).

next_steps.requires_info_note: A known-good board reading is strongly recommended — CPU VRM resistance is too board-specific to interpret alone.
